html:
A huge blast in the harbour of Halifax, Nova Scotia, on the morning of 6 December 1917. It was the largest man-made explosion in history until the first atomic bombs.

Halifax was a busy port for convoys carrying troops and supplies across the Atlantic during World War I. The French ship Mont-Blanc, loaded with explosives for the war in France, collided with the Norwegian ship Imo in the narrows of the harbour. Mont-Blanc caught fire, and crowds gathered to watch. About twenty minutes later it blew up.

The blast flattened the Richmond district, sent a tsunami into the shore and threw pieces of the ship kilometres away. At least 1,782 people were killed in Halifax and Dartmouth, and some 9,000 injured, many blinded by flying glass from people watching at windows. A blizzard the next day made rescue harder. Help poured in, especially from Boston, and every year since 1971 Nova Scotia has sent Boston a Christmas tree in thanks.
sum: A huge blast in the harbour of Halifax, Nova Scotia, on the morning of 6 December 1917. It was the largest man-made explosion in history until the first atomic bombs.
